collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A family wants to send their elder off the old way, with a night-long vigil fire: hold the vigil, or keep it short.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s grandfather has died, peacefully, at a great age. The family wants the old vigil: a fire kept burning beside him all night, with someone always awake, telling stories of his life. (friend) has offered to help keep the fire, but the village is exhausted from the harvest. How should the vigil go?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Family and friends take turns all night: an hour each, with a story each. By dawn, the stories have gone from solemn to funny to very, very funny, and (subject) has learned three things about (subject.his/her) grandfather (subject.he/she) is not sure (subject.he/she) wanted to know. The fire never goes out.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The family keeps the fire until midnight, then lets it burn down. (subject) stays on alone a little longer, talking quietly to (subject.his/her) grandfather. (friend) waits outside the firelight so (friend.he/she) is not alone.
